No.3.
 Order

The present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been preferred by the petitioner assailing the order dated 16.03.2018 passed by the learned First Additional Sessions Judge, Datia in Criminal Revision No.25 of 2014, whereby the said revision filed by the petitioner came to be dismissed and the order dated 03.02.2014 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Datia was affirmed.

By the said order dated 03.02.2014, the learned Magistrate had dismissed the complaint filed by the petitioner after holding that no prima facie case was made out for taking cognizance of the offences alleged.

Being aggrieved by the concurrent findings recorded by the courts below, the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7808 2 MCRC-36407-2018 petitioner has invoked the inherent jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking interference with the impugned orders.

The brief facts giving rise to the present petition are that the petitioner/complainant filed a complaint seeking registration of offences against respondents No.1 to 5 for the alleged commission of offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B and 34 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860.
It was alleged that the petitioner was the owner of agricultural land bearing Survey Nos. 286 and 290, comprising two plots ad-measuring 1.41 hectares, situated at village Dursada.

Out of the said land, the petitioner had sold 1.09 hectares to respondent No.1, Virendra Singh Dangi, by way of a registered sale deed dated 24.07.1999, while the remaining land continued to remain in the Ramprakash Kurmi vs Virendra Singh Dangi on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154493193/
1 ownership and possession of the petitioner.

sentences.text:
However, it was alleged that respondent No.1, in connivance with his wife, respondent No.2 Bharti, who was the Sarpanch of the village, along with respondent No.3 (Secretary) and respondent No.4 (Patwari), entered into a criminal conspiracy and,
by abusing their official position, fraudulently got the entire land ad-measuring 1.41 hectares of the aforesaid survey numbers mutated in favour of respondent No.1 through Resolution No.03 dated 20.08.2001.
For this purpose, a forged document in the form of Inquiry No.35 dated 01.07.2001 was allegedly prepared and relied upon.

The petitioner contended that he came to know about the said illegal mutation NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7808 3 MCRC-36407-2018 only on 28.06.2013 when he went to plough the remaining portion of his land and was stopped by respondent No.1, who claimed ownership over the entire land.

Thereafter, the petitioner obtained certified copies of the sale deed and mutation records, from which he allegedly discovered that the private respondents had fraudulently secured mutation of the entire land in their favour by using forged documents.
The petitioner thereafter submitted complaints before the concerned police station, the Superintendent of Police, Datia, and the Collector, Datia, but no action was taken.
Being aggrieved by such inaction, the petitioner filed a complaint before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Datia; however, the said complaint was dismissed vide order dated 03.02.2014.

Dissatisfied with the said order, the petitioner preferred a criminal revision before the First Additional Sessions Judge, Datia, which too came to be dismissed vide order dated 16.03.2018 affirming the order of the learned Magistrate.
Hence, the present petition.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the impugned orders passed by the courts below are illegal, arbitrary and contrary to the material available on record, and therefore deserve to be set aside, as they have failed to properly appreciate the allegations made in the complaint as well as the statements and documents produced by the petitioner during the preliminary inquiry.

The petitioner is the lawful owner of land bearing Survey Nos. 286 and 290 ad-measuring 1.41 hectares and had sold only 1.09 hectares of the said land to respondent NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:7808 4 MCRC-36407-2018 No.1, Virendra Singh Dangi, through a registered sale deed dated 24.07.1999, while the remaining portion of land continued to remain in the ownership and possession of the petitioner.

It is further submitted that respondent No.1, in connivance with respondent No.2 Bharti, who was the Sarpanch of the village, along with respondent No.3, the Secretary, and respondent No.4, the Patwari, entered into a criminal conspiracy and misused their official positions to get the entire land ad-measuring 1.41 hectares mutated in favour of respondent No.1 by preparing forged and fabricated documents.

Learned counsel contends that such mutation was obtained on the basis of a fabricated inquiry report and resolution, which clearly reflects the dishonest intention of the private respondents to cause wrongful loss to the petitioner and wrongful gain to themselves.

It is also submitted that the petitioner had no knowledge about the said fraudulent mutation and came to know about it only on 28.06.2013 when he went to cultivate the remaining portion of his land and was prevented by respondent No.1, who claimed ownership over the entire land.

Immediately thereafter, the petitioner obtained certified copies of the relevant documents, which revealed that the private respondents had illegally and fraudulently got the entire land mutated in favour of respondent No.1.

Learned counsel submits that despite submitting complaints before the Ramprakash Kurmi vs Virendra Singh Dangi on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154493193/
2 concerned police authorities and higher officials, no action was taken, which compelled the petitioner to approach the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7808 5 MCRC-36407-2018 court by filing a complaint.

sentences.text: Learned counsel further submits that the learned Magistrate erred in dismissing the complaint without properly considering the statements recorded under Section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the documentary evidence produced by the petitioner.

It is contended that at the stage of taking cognizance, the court is only required to see whether a prima facie case is made out,
and a detailed appreciation of evidence is not required.
However, the learned Magistrate rejected the complaint by adopting an approach as if the matter was being finally adjudicated after trial.

It is also argued that the revisional court committed a similar error in affirming the order of the Magistrate without properly examining the material placed on record and without considering that the allegations made in the complaint clearly disclose the commission of offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
The findings recorded by the courts below are perverse and based on an incorrect appreciation of the facts of the case.

On these submissions, learned counsel submits that the impugned orders passed by the courts below are liable to be set aside and the complaint filed by the petitioner deserves to be restored with a direction to the trial court to proceed in accordance with law.

Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor appearing for the State as well as learned counsel for respondent No.3 have vehemently opposed NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7808 6 MCRC-36407-2018 the present petition and supported the impugned orders passed by the courts below.

It is submitted that the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Datia, after conducting a proper inquiry under Section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and upon due consideration of the statements of the complainant and the material placed on record, rightly concluded that no prima facie case was made out against the respondents for the offences alleged under Sections 420,
467, 468, 471, 120-B and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

It is further contended that the revisional court, after independently examining the entire record, concurred with the findings recorded by the trial court and affirmed the order dated 03.02.2014, finding no illegality, impropriety or jurisdictional error therein.

It is thus submitted that both the courts below have recorded concurrent findings of fact based on proper appreciation of the material available on record and the petitioner has failed to demonstrate any perversity or patent illegality in the impugned orders warranting interference by this Court in exercise of its inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Accordingly, it is prayed that the present petition, being devoid of merit,
deserves to be dismissed.

This Court, after hearing the learned counsel for the parties and perusing the material available on record, finds that the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Datia had duly conducted an inquiry in accordance with law under Section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and had considered the statements of the complainant as well NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7808 7 MCRC-36407-2018 as the material produced in support of the complaint.

Upon such consideration,
the Magistrate arrived at a conclusion that the essential ingredients of the offences alleged under Ramprakash Kurmi vs Virendra Singh Dangi on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154493193/
3 Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B and 34 of the Indian Penal Code were not made out and that no prima facie case was disclosed against the respondents, and therefore the complaint was rightly dismissed by order dated 03.02.2014.

sentences.text: It is further noted that the petitioner had challenged the said order by filing a criminal revision before the First Additional Sessions Judge, Datia and the revisional court, after independently examining the record and the reasoning assigned by the learned Magistrate, concurred with the findings recorded by the trial court and held that the complainant had failed to place any cogent material demonstrating that the respondents had prepared forged documents or had committed cheating or any other criminal offence.

The revisional court thus found that the order passed by the Magistrate did not suffer from any illegality, impropriety or jurisdictional error and accordingly dismissed the revision by order dated 16.03.2018 affirming the order of the Magistrate.

While considering the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, this observes that both the courts below had recorded concurrent findings of fact after due appreciation of the material available on record.

The inherent powers of this Court under Section 482 of the Code are to be exercised sparingly and only in cases where there is a manifest illegality, perversity or abuse of the process of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7808 8 MCRC-36407-2018 the court.

In the present case, the petitioner has not been able to demonstrate that the findings recorded by the courts below suffer from any perversity, illegality or material irregularity warranting interference in the exercise of inherent jurisdiction.

This Court also observes that the courts below had rightly concluded that the complaint and the statements recorded during the inquiry did not disclose the essential ingredients of the offences alleged and the petitioner had failed to establish any prima facie case against the respondents.
In view of the aforesaid, this Court holds that the impugned orders passed by the courts below are well-reasoned and do not call for any interference.

Since both the courts below have concurrently held that no case is made out for proceeding against the respondents and no illegality or perversity has been pointed out in the said findings, this Court finds no ground to exercise its inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Consequently, the present petition being devoid of merit is dismissed.

(MILIND RAMESH PHADKE) JUDGE pwn*
